name: Island Pacific Distributors
old_description: Founded on October 2, 1978 by Barbara and Leon Wolfley, Island Pacific Distributors (IPD) began our humble beginnings at our King Street location, opening our doors to customers as a Wholesale Hardware and Locksmith Supply Company. IPD concentrated on supplying high security keys and locks for perimeter doors on many of the high-rise condominiums being built during the high-rise boom in Waikiki and along the Ala Wai Corridor. Along with condominiums, we sold to many of the local retail establishments of the time including McDonalds, Liberty House, Gibson’s, Handyman Hardware, Holiday Mart Hardware, Ben Franklin Stores, & J.C. Penny’s.
about:
Island Pacific Distributors was founded on October 2, 1978, by Barbara and Leon Wolfley in Honolulu, Hawaii. The company began as a wholesale hardware and locksmith supply operation on King Street, serving the high-rise condominium boom in Waikiki and the Ala Wai corridor. In 2014, the business transitioned to an employee stock ownership plan (ESOP), making it fully employee-owned.

Today, IPD operates from a 35,000-square-foot facility in the Iwilei area of Oahu that includes offices, a warehouse, a showroom, and a steel door and frame fabrication shop. The shop is the only Warnock Hersey–marked facility in the state certified by Intertek to build and modify Assa Abloy’s Curries hollow metal doors and frames. The company distributes doors, frames, finish hardware, security products, and specialty building products, and also provides consultation, design, specification writing, installation, maintenance, electronic access control, and in-house locksmith services.

IPD serves architects, general contractors, and facility managers across Hawaii’s hospitality, commercial construction, government, and luxury residential sectors. Notable projects include the Allure Waikiki, Moana Surfrider, Sheraton Moana Surfrider, Four Seasons Resort Lanai, Disney Aulani Resort, Hokua, and the Kapolei Judiciary Complex. The company also lists medical, dental, and vision insurance among its served industries.

name: J & O Plastics
old_description: J&O Plastics specializes in plastic injection molding solutions for plastic shipping products and the logistics industry.
about:
J & O Plastics operates from a 250,000-square-foot production and warehousing facility in Rittman, Ohio, located in the state's retail distribution corridor. The company was founded in 1982 by Oscar and Christine Gross as an injection molding supplier to the Mr. Coffee Company and remains family-owned.

The company specializes in clear plastic injection molding, notably pioneering a proprietary process for straight PET that yields BPA-free, cosmetically clear parts at low cost. It also molds acrylic, polypropylene, SAN, crystal styrene, PVC, ABS, LDPE, and HDPE. Services encompass custom and large-part injection molding, in-line assembly, kitting, packaging, barcoding, SKU and inventory management, warehousing, and direct shipment to major retailers and Amazon FBA.

J & O serves household, industrial, agricultural, medical, and shipping/logistics markets.

The company differentiates itself through its early adoption of straight PET molding—one of few U.S. firms offering it—along with automation-driven competitive pricing, a lean facility that keeps scrap under 1 percent, and a commitment to same-day shipping and delivery from its centrally located Ohio plant.

name: J & R Senior Sheetmetal, Inc.
old_description: J&R Senior Sheetmetal Inc., a family-owned and operated business in Westerly, Rhode Island, specializes in custom copper work. Serving most of Rhode Island, including Block Island, we bring 30 years of metal experience across three generations and over 40 years of roofing expertise to ensure your home stays dry. We take pride in tackling the unique challenges of building coastal homes and prioritize providing quality service and products that withstand the harsh New England weather. If you can build it, we can cover it (in metal, of course). Over the past 30 years, we have earned a reputation for using innovative approaches to help our clients achieve their goals. We provide exceptional customer service and work closely with builders, roofers, and homeowners to fully understand their needs and expectations.
about:
Located in Westerly, Rhode Island, J & R Senior Sheetmetal, Inc. is a family-owned and operated business built on three generations of metalworking experience. The company traces its roots to over 40 years of roofing expertise and three decades of custom metal fabrication, though a specific founding year is not publicly disclosed.

The shop specializes in custom copper work, producing a range of architectural sheet metal components including roof vents, wall vents, drip edges, valleys, window and door pans, shower pans, step flashing, chimney caps, scuppers, and radius flashing. It also fabricates standing seam roof systems, flat-pounded panels, cupolas, chimney through-flashings, and radius roofs, with a dedicated line for .032 aluminum standing seam. In addition to fabrication, the company distributes Wuko tools and PREFA products and offers pre-packaged standing seam roof bundles that include high-temperature ice and water shield, wall flashings, drip edge, panels, clips, screws, Z-bar, and ridge caps. Production relies on a mix of antique hand tools and modern machinery, with an emphasis on quick turnaround.

The primary customers are builders, roofers, and homeowners throughout Rhode Island, including Block Island, with a focus on coastal construction that must withstand harsh New England weather. The company’s portfolio spans residential roofing, custom flashing, and specialty metal accents for both new builds and renovations.

J & R Senior Sheetmetal distinguishes itself through its multi-generational family ownership, deep roofing heritage, and a commitment to American-made products. The firm highlights its innovative approaches to coastal building challenges, personalized customer service, and the ability to deliver both standard and intricate custom pieces on short lead times.

name: J E Fifer Sheet Metal Fabricators Inc
old_description: Fifer Sheet Metal offers a variety of precision-based sheet metal services, including manufacturing custom-built machinery and fabricating precision parts. Backed by decades of experience, we strive to exceed the needs of our customers with employees equipped with expert craftsmanship and special attention to details.
about:
J.E. Fifer Sheet Metal Fabricators operates from a 30,000-square-foot facility in Richmond, Virginia. The company was founded in 1986 by James and Judy Fifer and remains family-owned, with their son Jason T. Fifer now serving as president.

The shop specializes in precision sheet metal fabrication, producing custom parts, assemblies, and complete machinery. Capabilities include CNC laser cutting, punching, and bending; TIG and MIG welding on aluminum, stainless steel, and mild steel; CNC PEM insertion; saw cutting; rolling; shearing up to 10 feet long and 1/4 inch thick in mild steel; and deburring on a Costa Metal Finishing machine. The facility also houses CNC and manual mills and lathes for precision machining, plus in-house shrink-packaging equipment that allows the company to deliver both fabricated components and proprietary packaging systems under one roof.

Fifer serves customers needing custom-built machinery, equipment upgrades, replacement parts, and shrink-packaging solutions. Its work supports industrial OEMs and manufacturers requiring fabricated metal components and integrated packaging equipment, though the company does not publicly list specific industry verticals.

The founders established the business on a commitment to quality products, timely communication, and on-time delivery — values that Jason Fifer says drive a mission of “ever-increasing satisfaction and sustainability through leadership, consistency, and integrity.” Repeat business is cited as the cornerstone of the company’s success.

old_description: Since 1994, JR Plastics & Machining, Inc. has provided custom vacuum forming for North America. Utilizing reliable and accurate equipment, we produce quality parts with very little down time.
about:
JR Plastics & Machining, Inc. operates from Lowesville, Virginia, in the Blue Ridge Mountains about 25 miles south of Charlottesville. In 1998 the business added a full CNC machine shop, bringing mold making and secondary machining in-house.

The shop provides custom vacuum forming, hotwire bending, CNC machining, and engineering design services. Vacuum forming capacity reaches 24 by 50 by 9 inches deep in sheet up to 0.250 inch thick, using materials such as PETG, PVC, ABS, polycarbonate (Kydex), polystyrene, acrylic, and HDPE. CNC machining handles parts up to 50 by 100 by 9 inches in aluminum, brass, and stainless steel. Equipment includes HAAS mills, lathes, and routers, plus custom-built forming and bending machines maintained by the team.

Customers span medical, electronics, food packaging, and sports performance sectors, with the company noting satisfied clients across the United States. The firm emphasizes prototypes, short runs, and large-scale production, all managed under one roof.

The owners position the business on single-source convenience: clients work directly with Trent or Schneider from quote to delivery, and the in-house equipment fabrication allows rapid repairs to keep production on schedule.

old_description: We specialize in transitioning injection molding projects to reach the next level in development and production.
about:
J&L Plastic Molding operates from Wallingford, Connecticut, where it runs a molding facility across two buildings.

The shop specializes in injection molding, prototype and production tooling, insert molding, and tool transfer services. Its equipment lineup includes 28 injection molding machines with clamp forces from 28 to 385 tons and shot capacities of 0.6 to 24 ounces, enabling production of parts in engineering-grade thermoplastics such as PEEK, Ultem, Radel, and other high-performance resins.

J&L primarily serves medical device manufacturers, with LeMaitre Vascular recognized as a key customer—the company received LeMaitre's Supplier of the Year award for quality, delivery, innovation, and collaboration. The firm's ISO 13485:2016 certification supports its work in regulated medical applications.

The company emphasizes its ability to transition projects from development to production, maintain schedule-driven delivery, and process high-performance resins. Its tool transfer process allows customers to move existing tooling into J&L's production system with minimal disruption.

about:
J-Tech Construction and Solar was founded in 2004 in Lincoln, Nebraska.

The company provides residential and commercial roofing, metal siding, window and door installation, seamless gutter systems, and solar panel installation. J-Tech fabricates its own metal roofing and siding components in-house, allowing for custom fit and tighter quality control. The firm also uses drone technology for roof assessments. Its service area covers much of Nebraska, plus parts of Iowa, Kansas, South Dakota, and Missouri.

J-Tech serves residential homeowners and commercial property owners across its service territory. The company works with insurance restoration projects and offers financing for large exterior projects. Its customer base includes homeowners in Lincoln, Omaha, Grand Island, and surrounding communities, as well as commercial clients needing roofing, siding, or solar installations.

J-Tech differentiates itself through in-house metal fabrication, which ensures precise fit and quality control; drone roof inspections that provide clear documentation before work begins; and a single-contractor model that handles roofing, siding, windows, doors, gutters, and solar without subcontractors. The company highlights its 20-plus years in business, certifications as a ProVia Partner and James Hardie Contractor Alliance Partner, warranty-backed installations, and free inspections with no obligation.

The company points to Anguiano’s patent‑pending screen‑printing techniques and his two decades of experience as key differentiators, along with Boesel’s product‑development expertise and Bartosiak’s precision in registration. about:
JCS Technologies Inc. operates from Las Vegas, Nevada, where it was founded in 2011.

The company specializes in the full lifecycle of wire harnesses: design assistance, rapid prototyping with no minimum order quantities, and low-volume manufacturing. Its recent move to a larger facility supports a commitment to on-time delivery. Every unit is 100% tested before shipment, and the firm backs its work with a 0% Failure Rate Guarantee that includes free replacement within 48 hours. Headcount and annual volume figures are not disclosed, but the business emphasizes fast turnaround on small-to-medium runs rather than high-volume production.

JCS serves four primary sectors: casino gaming equipment, renewable energy (controllers, generators), industrial electronics (consumer devices, kiosks, ATMs, computers), and amusement systems (audio, video, control, and payment integration). Named customers include Light & Wonder and Asahi Seiko, both cited for the speed and quality of delivered harnesses.

The company was started to end an era of acceptable fail rates. Its stated differentiators are a zero-failure guarantee, no minimums, quick turnaround on low-volume orders, individual product testing, and compliance with UL and RoHS standards.

The shop produces a range of handcrafted wood goods including cutting boards (end-grain, personalized, and striped designs in black walnut, cherry, and maple), flags and wall decor, holiday decorations, and offers custom furniture repair services. Work is characterized as original, built to last, and reliant on quality materials, attention to detail, and patience. No facility size, headcount, or production volumes are disclosed.

old_description: Founded in 2010, JPM Fabrication is a Veteran-Owned (VOSB) and Family-Operated business in NW Arkansas. We started from humble beginnings and have been blessed to gain the trust of our customers across the country.
about:
JPM Steel Fabrication was founded in 2010 in Bella Vista, Arkansas, by James P. McGary, an Army veteran who served in Iraq from 2003 to 2005. After years working in concrete construction and storage-solution installation, McGary saw a shortage of skilled steel fabricators in the region and opened his own shop. The business is certified as a Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB) and is family-operated; McGary’s wife Erin, also an Army veteran, helps run the household while his brothers often lead installation crews.

The company designs, fabricates, and installs custom tension-fabric storage buildings—often called hoop sheds or fabric domes—for bulk materials such as grain, sand, salt, hay, and equipment. Beyond the fabric structures, JPM provides full-service maintenance, repair, retrofit (including “retrodomes” on existing foundations), cover replacement, and building relocation. The shop has grown from a single crew to multiple full-time steel fabricators, installation specialists, and office staff, and it also produces consumer items like steel benches and fire pits while performing general contracting for municipalities and large-scale commercial customizations.

JPM serves agriculture (farms, fisheries, grain storage), government and municipal agencies (salt and sand storage, maintenance buildings), waste and recycling facilities, aviation (aircraft hangars), mining operations, equestrian centers, port and intermodal terminals, and railroad depots. Customers range from individual farmers and construction companies to city, state, and federal agencies across the continental United States.

The founders started the business to fill a local gap in skilled steel fabrication and to carry on a tradition of tradesmanship. The company emphasizes a “cut materials, not corners” philosophy, with the founder personally involved in every project from design through installation. Differentiators include a 25-year warranty on fabricated buildings, two years of included maintenance, engineer-approved designs, and a commitment to inspecting every component before it leaves the shop.

Jordan Manufacturing Company was founded in 1975 by Dave Jordan in the basement of his Peoria, Illinois home. A dropship program launched in 1999 supports online retailers, while custom product development helps brands differentiate their assortments.

The company emphasizes ethical and sustainable practices. All facilities are Sedex members and SMETA compliant, and the business earned Global Recycle Standard (GRS) certification in 2022. Vertical integration and proprietary equipment are cited as the basis for competitive pricing and fast turnaround, allowing Jordan to offer customized solutions without sacrificing quality.

name: Kamuela Hardwoods
old_description: Kamuela Hardwoods in Kamuela, HI specializes in reclaimed Hawaiian timber, live-edge slabs, and premium hardwood lumber for furniture makers, woodworkers, instrument builders, and artisans. Our sawmill salvages urban and felled trees, turning them into high-quality wood while supporting sustainable forestry practices. We offer over 30 Hawaiian and exotic
about:
Kamuela Hardwoods operates from Waimea on the island of Hawaii, where it runs a sawmill dedicated to reclaiming urban and felled trees. The company was formed as a partnership between an arborist and a woodworker, with co‑owners Alex Woodbury and Joshua Greenspan (an ISA‑certified arborist) the operation.

The mill processes over 30 Hawaiian and exotic hardwood species — including koa, monkeypod, mango, Norfolk pine, lychee, eucalyptus, and ohia — into live‑edge slabs, kiln‑dried lumber, and bowl blanks. Logs are sawn on site, dried in a kiln to ensure stability, and every by‑product is repurposed: offcuts become utility lumber, sawdust turns to mulch, and slash is used for garden materials. The facility runs on locally produced bio‑diesel and follows a strict recycling program. A team of eight handles milling, woodworking, sales, and marketing, shipping products across Hawaii, the continental U.S., and internationally.

The lumber serves furniture makers, woodworkers, instrument builders, artisans, cabinetmakers, and builders seeking distinctive Hawaiian woods for custom projects, countertops, flooring, and musical instruments.

The founders frame the business as a response to waste: “We are trying to do something different, we don’t want to unnecessarily remove a tree for any reason,” says Woodbury. Greenspan adds, “It’s unfortunate when a tree has to come down, but in a sense, we’re giving it a new life.” The zero‑waste model and bio‑diesel power underscore a mission to salvage timber that would otherwise be burned or landfilled.

Clark cites a lifetime guarantee on every piece as a core differentiator, reflecting a commitment to durability. His design philosophy draws on the fluid forms of nature, and the Sam Maloof rocking-chair lineage informs the sculptural comfort of his seating. The business was built on the desire to create functional art that brings the peace of the outdoors into daily life.

The shop stocks a broad range of products including abrasives, router bits, saw blades, carving and turning tools, cabinet-making supplies, finishing products, hardware, power tools, dust-collection equipment, sharpening systems, safety gear, and both common and exotic lumber. It also carries CNC machines and accessories, such as Amana CNC bit sets. In addition to sales, the store runs in-store woodworking classes led by staff and guest instructors for all skill levels, and provides meeting space for several regional woodworking clubs.

Customers include hobbyists, professional woodworkers, woodturners, carvers, and pyrography artists. The Hickory store hosts monthly gatherings for the Southeastern Pyrography Association, the North Carolina Woodturners Association, the Catawba Valley Woodcarvers, and the Western Piedmont Woodcrafters, offering a venue for demonstrations, show-and-tell, and fellowship.

The company emphasizes hands-on learning and community, promoting its classes as a way for makers to build projects under expert guidance and its club partnerships as a hub for local woodworking culture. A weekly updated specials flyer and a newsletter called "Sawdust" keep customers informed on sales, classes, and club events.

name: Knectiv
old_description: Hardware manufacturing, managed from engineering to production.
about:
Knectiv is based in Austin, Texas. The company was founded by Nicholas J. Frank, who serves as CEO, and Michael Lally, co-founder. Frank brought over a decade of experience in the Swiss electronics industry before establishing Knectiv to provide managed manufacturing services for complex hardware.

Knectiv provides end-to-end hardware commercialization, spanning product engineering, PCB manufacturing and assembly, plastic injection molding, conformal coating, press-fit and fine-pitch component placement (CSP, CCGA, BGA, 01005), systems integration, sourcing, and turnkey manufacturing. The firm coordinates global production with U.S.-side accountability and China-side execution, handling production planning, quality, packaging, and scale-up for clients.

The company serves industrial, medical, consumer, automotive, audio, and connected-hardware markets. Customers include GETS (Swiss medical-device manufacturer), Merging Technologies Switzerland, Zefon International (air-quality measurement systems), and CEBI Micromotors Switzerland (automotive sub-assemblies). Portfolio projects range from microhematocrit centrifuges and LFIA readers to endoscopic insufflators, blood-pressure monitors, and Bluetooth-enabled pedals.

Knectiv emphasizes a unified approach: a single point of contact, consistent quality across the manufacturing chain, and efficiency gains by consolidating multiple vendors. Its stated mission centers on sustainability, innovation, integrity, collaboration, and excellence, aiming to make hardware development easier while delivering positive societal and environmental impact.

name: Kulite Semiconductor Products
old_description: Visit the Reference Library for Handbooks, Manuals, Installation Instructions, Technical Papers and More
about:
Kulite Semiconductor Products was founded in 1959 by Dr. Anthony D. Kurtz in Leonia, New Jersey, where the company maintains a three-building, 200,000-square-foot campus. A physicist with degrees from MIT, Dr. Kurtz had previously worked at Honeywell before returning to New Jersey to start the business. The family-founded, woman-owned enterprise is now led by his widow, Nora Kurtz, who assumed leadership after his death in 2010.

The company designs and manufactures pressure transducers and sensors for extreme environments, offering pressure ranges from 1 to 60,000 PSI, operating temperatures from -320°F to 932°F, and resistance to vibration up to 100g. Its product line includes unamplified and amplified outputs, submersible transmitters, pressure switches, and redundant sensor configurations. Kulite holds over 400 patents and produces both standard catalog items and thousands of custom designs.

Kulite serves aerospace and defense, automotive (including Formula One and IndyCar testing), marine, space, and process-control industries. Its transducers are used on commercial aircraft such as the Boeing 747, naval vessels, oil-exploration equipment, and weather balloons. The company describes itself as the world's largest supplier of aerospace transducers.

Dr. Kurtz established the company to become the worldwide expert in transducer technology, emphasizing long-term employee retention, university partnerships, and continuous R&D investment. The firm cites its patent portfolio, custom-engineering capability, and woman-owned, family-led structure as key differentiators.

Dave White left his previous job convinced he could deliver greater value to customers than the market offered, and the couple built the business around that principle. Now operating as Kyana Packaging Solutions, the company remains headquartered in Louisville.

The company operates across three divisions. Kyana Packaging Solutions distributes a broad line of packaging supplies — corrugated boxes, tapes, poly bags, stretch and shrink films, cushioning, cold-chain materials, labels, strapping, safety and janitorial products — and sells packaging equipment. ASR Solutions provides third-party logistics, kitting, and assembly services, turning components into ready-to-ship kits. Bethlehem Die Cutting produces custom die-cut parts for specialized packaging and industrial applications. The firm also offers a packaging assessment program to help clients optimize their packaging spend and performance.

old_description: 京セラの電子部品事業の一翼を担うKYOCERA AVX Components Corporation（本社：米国）は、電子デバイス関連製品の強固な技術基盤と豊富なラインアップを有し、開発から製造、販売までをグローバルに展開しています。
about:
Kyocera Electronic Devices LLC operates from Fountain Inn, South Carolina, as the U.S. entity of KYOCERA AVX Components Corporation, a Japanese manufacturer of electronic components. The business serves as the local face of a global organization that develops, manufactures, and sells electronic devices worldwide, leveraging the parent company’s deep technical foundation and broad product portfolio.

The company manufactures a wide range of passive and electromechanical components. Its product lines include multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCC), polymer and tantalum capacitors, board-to-board, FPC/FFC, wire-to-board, and memory card connectors, as well as timing devices such as crystal oscillators, SPXOs, and TCXOs. It also produces SAW filters, duplexers, and multiplexers, along with sensors and circuit protection devices. The operation spans design through volume production, though specific facility size and headcount are not disclosed.

Customers span automotive, consumer electronics, industrial, data-center, robotics, aerospace, and telecommunications sectors. In automotive, the company supplies AEC-Q200-qualified parts for battery-management systems (wBMS) and safety applications. Consumer applications include smartphones, wearables, gaming systems, and communication modules. Industrial and data-center customers use its components in AI servers, base stations, and general automation equipment.

The organization emphasizes a seamless flow from development to manufacturing and sales on a global scale. It highlights multi-band SAW solutions that save space in GNSS and positioning devices, ultra-miniature low-power timing devices for smart rings and medical instruments, and high-speed 0.5 mm pitch floating connectors for next-generation data transmission.

old_description: In 1885, civil engineer Leprilete Sweet founded L. Sweet & Company, in the Olneyville section of Providence, RI.
about:
L. Sweet Lumber Company Inc. has operated from Providence, Rhode Island since 1885, when civil engineer Leprilete Sweet founded L. Sweet & Company in the city's Olneyville section. Sweet soon purchased a wooden frame building from the Church of the Messiah, moved it to Harris Avenue for railroad access, and established the storefront that remains in use today. Now in its fifth generation, the business remains family‑owned and locally operated.

The company stocks a broad range of building materials: framing and finish lumber sourced from domestic and international forests, an extensive inventory of historical moulding profiles specific to the Providence area, interior and exterior doors, windows, skylights, hardwood flooring, TimberTech/Azek composite decking and railing, cedar shingles and clapboard siding, and general building supplies. A showroom displays samples and literature, and the staff provides blade sharpening, key cutting, and lock keying services. A fleet of trucks handles delivery across Southern New England.

L. Sweet Lumber serves contractors, homeowners, and historical‑restoration projects throughout Southern New England. The sales team offers personalized estimates, site visits, and product consultation, while the back office manages trade‑credit accounts and invoicing. The company also runs a contractor‑referral network for homeowners and supplies evaluated leads to its trade customers.

The firm emphasizes that its 140‑year commitment to service, selection, quality, and competitive pricing drives its approach.

old_description: To become the leading provider of engineering, fabrication, and technical services in the Rocky Mountain region, distinguished by our uncompromising standards in quality, advanced innovation, and customer-centric solutions.
about:
Based in Douglas, Wyoming, L&L Fabrication Inc operates as an ASME-certified pressure vessel shop serving the Rocky Mountain region.

The shop holds ASME U, R, and VR stamps, allowing it to fabricate, repair, and alter coded pressure vessels to specification. Its capabilities include coded vessel fabrication and repair, engineering support, piping fabrication up to 72 inches in diameter, certified crane and rigging services, customized hauling, and on-site field services for oil and gas operations. Processes encompass coded welding, plasma cutting of conductive metals such as steel, stainless steel, aluminum, brass, and copper, as well as heavy industrial fabrication of skidded process equipment, separator vessels, and gas production equipment.

L&L Fabrication primarily serves the oil and gas sector, including pipeline operations, gas production facilities, and upstream and midstream projects. The company provides custom metal fabrication in Wyoming and industrial fabrication contractor services throughout Colorado, supporting customers with heavy industrial fabrication and on-site support.

The company states its vision is to become the provider of engineering, fabrication, and technical services in the Rocky Mountain region, distinguished by uncompromising quality standards, advanced innovation, and customer-centric solutions. Core values cited include integrity, innovation, quality, and efficacy, with an emphasis on meeting deadlines and maintaining site safety.

Primary customers work in oil and gas, electric utility, refining, and petrochemical industries. The company sells through a network of distributors and directly via its e-commerce site, serving both men and women with modern, comfort-focused designs. Trade association membership underscores its industry standing.

LAPCO emphasizes a service-oriented approach, promoting excellent customer support, pain-free inventory acquisition for distributors, and responsive custom order fulfillment. The brand positions itself on safety, reliability, and purpose, aiming to deliver workwear that helps wearers feel safe, work smart, and look good.

name: LadyBug Technologies, LLC
old_description: Fast, Accurate & Traceable Power Sensors, 4 kHz to 67 GHz with 86dB Dynamic Range
about:
LadyBug Technologies, LLC was founded in 2004 in Santa Rosa, California, by microwave engineers Richard Hawkins and Jon Sigler. The company relocated to Boise, Idaho in 2021, doubling its facility space and expanding manufacturing capacity by 30 percent. Hawkins serves as president, bringing four decades of RF and microwave test and measurement experience, while Sigler, a retired vice president and U.S. Marine veteran, contributed software and firmware expertise.

The company designs, develops, and manufactures a broad line of USB power sensors that function as complete, self-contained power measurement solutions without a separate meter. Covering 4 kHz to 67 GHz with 86 dB dynamic range, the product portfolio includes true RMS, peak/pulse/average, pulse profiling, and small form factor sensors, as well as the LB5900 series with optional I2C/SPI interfaces and Linux compatibility. LadyBug also provides NIST-traceable calibration services and power sensor rentals.

LadyBug’s sensors serve the microwave and RF test industry, automated test equipment (ATE) systems, defense applications, and portable or compact test setups. Customers use them for general-purpose RF power testing, military radar, and programmatic test environments such as LabVIEW and VEE.

The founders started the company to build a better product at a better price in the United States. LadyBug differentiates itself with patented NoZero NoCal technology that eliminates user zeroing and reduces drift, and with an integrated sensor architecture that removes the uncertainty of a separate meter. All analog and digitization circuitry is calibrated as a single unit under an ISO 9001:2015 quality system.

The company is a member of the American Association of Meat Processors (AAMP) and the Wisconsin Association of Meat Processors (WAMP), exhibiting at both national and state conventions to stay close to customer needs.

about:
LeVic Plastics was founded in 1971 by Leslie "Bill" Stober and Vic Mathis in a garage in Grandview, Missouri, initially focusing on prototype molding for manufacturers. The company incorporated and moved to a dedicated facility in Grandview as demand grew, with Ron Knight becoming a partial owner before taking sole ownership in 1990. Bob Knight later purchased the business, continuing its customer-focused manufacturing approach.

Today LeVic operates as a full-service custom injection molder with in-house tooling and secondary operations under one roof. The facility runs 10 Shibaura (Toshiba) presses ranging from 55 to 250 tons, capable of holding tolerances to ±0.001 inch and producing runs from a single piece to over 100,000 parts. Services span mold design, CNC machining of aluminum and steel tooling, insert molding, color matching, and secondary processes such as sonic welding, pad printing, hot stamping, assembly, and packaging.

The company serves manufacturers across medical, aerospace, electronics, oil and gas, industrial automation, machinery, and packaging sectors. Engineers, buyers, and supply chain teams engage LeVic for prototype development, low-to-mid volume production, and ongoing manufacturing support, often consolidating multiple suppliers into a single point of accountability.

LeVic emphasizes its "One-Vendor Advantage," combining engineering-driven DFM support, certified quality systems (ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100D), no minimum order quantities, and quote turnaround within two to three business days to simplify supply chains and ensure repeatable quality from first article through long-term production.

name: Leprino Foods Company
old_description: We started in 1950 as a small family-run grocery store in Denver, Colorado. Today, Leprino is proud to be the world’s largest producer of mozzarella cheese and a leading manufacturer of whey protein, lactose, micellar casein and other high-quality dairy ingredients.
about:
Leprino Foods Company began in 1950 as a small family-run grocery store in Denver, Colorado, when Mike Leprino Sr. started making mozzarella cheese by hand in a back room for his family's corner market. The business incorporated as Leprino Cheese Manufacturing Company in the 1960s and adopted the Leprino Foods Company name in the 1970s, remaining family-owned throughout its growth.

Today the company is the world's largest producer of mozzarella cheese and a manufacturer of whey protein, lactose, micellar casein, and other dairy ingredients. Its proprietary processes include the patented "Same Day Dice" method that turns fresh milk into cheese in four hours, and Quality-Locked Cheese that is individually quick-frozen to preserve peak flavor. Operations span manufacturing facilities on three continents, including a 640,000-square-foot plant in Lemoore, California, with over 1,100 employees, and a global headcount exceeding 5,000. Products reach more than 70 countries.

Leprino serves food and nutrition brands worldwide, from major pizza chains and foodservice operators to consumer-packaged-goods manufacturers. A strategic alliance with Dairy Farmers of America secures milk supply, while joint ventures in Europe, Latin America, and Asia Pacific extend its reach. The company also entered the direct-to-consumer market with the Ascent® Protein brand.

name: Liberate Medical
old_description: VentFree contracts the expiratory muscles during mechanical ventilation to keep them active.
about:
Liberate Medical is based in Crestwood, Kentucky. The company develops and manufactures the VentFree Respiratory Muscle Stimulator, a non-invasive neuromuscular electrical stimulation device designed to contract the abdominal wall muscles in synchrony with exhalation during mechanical ventilation.

The VentFree system uses proprietary stimulation technology that can be initiated from the first day of mechanical ventilation, even while patients are sedated or delirious, without requiring patient cooperation. The device is CE marked for sale throughout the European Economic Area and holds U.S. FDA Emergency Use Authorization to reduce disuse atrophy of the abdominal wall muscles, which may shorten the duration of mechanical ventilation in adult patients, including those with COVID-19.

Liberate Medical serves the critical care and respiratory care markets, targeting hospitals and intensive care units that manage mechanically ventilated patients. Clinical evidence from a pilot randomized controlled trial published in Critical Care (2019) demonstrated that patients receiving VentFree stimulation experienced shorter mechanical ventilation duration and reduced ICU length of stay compared to placebo.

The company positions its technology as a breakthrough approach to preparing patients for weaning from day one of ventilation, aiming to reduce abdominal muscle atrophy—a factor associated with weaning failure and delayed extubation—and potentially lower morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs.

Pieces are designed to be well made, beautifully designed, and built to last, with lead times of 10 to 16 weeks for custom orders.

MSP Manufacturing operates from Bloomington, Indiana, where it was founded in 1943 by machinists focused on avionics and defense work. The company has remained multi-generational, passing from father to son, and in 2020 Johnny Goode — an Army National Guard veteran with a background in SWAT and law enforcement — became president, steering the shop toward modern automation while retaining its legacy craftsmanship.

The shop provides precision machining, 5-axis milling, 6-axis turning with live tooling, fabrication, welding, mil-spec coating, assembly, and inspection under one roof. Its equipment includes 3- and 5-axis CNC mills with pallet changers, a 6-axis lathe, CMMs, and an AI-assisted CAM system that cuts programming time by up to 80%. Work ranges from single prototypes to production runs in aluminum, steel, brass, titanium, plastics, and Inconel, all tracked through ProShop ERP for full traceability.

MSP serves defense, armory, aviation, medical, and contract-manufacturing customers. Its parts have flown on programs for Boeing, Curtiss-Wright, Bell Helicopter, Gulfstream, and Honeywell, and it supports defense startups and OEMs such as Simtek, Freedom Aero Service, and Ripcord Industries.

The company emphasizes “tight tolerances, zero drama, and people who care,” positioning itself as a partner for high-stakes, high-spec work rather than the largest shop. Veteran-led leadership, in-house finishing and assembly, and a culture of accountability are cited as differentiators.

name: Majors Plastics Inc.
old_description: Majors Plastics is a leading provider of precision injection molding solutions, offering high and medium volume production of tightly-toleranced components with exacting quality standards, supported by decades of technical expertise and state-of-the-art manufacturing infrastructure.
about:
Majors Plastics Inc. was founded in 1953 by Ben Pfeiffer and Eli Dahir in Omaha, Nebraska. The company began as an injection molding operation and moved to its current Plant One location in 1968. In 2013, after a gradual transition, it became a 100 percent employee-owned ESOP, a structure that now governs its corporate culture and long-term planning.

Today the company runs four molding facilities—three in Omaha totaling over 300,000 square feet with more than 120 molding machines, and one in Reynosa, Mexico, with 128,000 square feet and 36 machines. Its core capabilities include precision injection molding, true two-shot molding, overmolding, insert molding, and ISO Class-7 cleanroom molding with laminar HEPA-controlled airflow. Secondary services cover ultrasonic welding, heat staking, pad printing, painting, manual assembly, and custom packaging, supported by in-house engineering and tool-room resources. Approximately 500 employees handle high- and medium-volume production runs.

Its customer base includes 3M, which has recognized the company multiple times as a Supplier of the Year, and BD, which named it a Supply Chain Excellence Supplier of the Year. Earlier diversification brought energy-related products, thermoset tableware, and rigid computer-disc preparatory work, but the current focus remains on tightly toleranced components for regulated industries.

The company attributes its differentiation to its employee-ownership model, a disciplined ISO 9001:2015 quality system that targets Cpk values above 1.33 and AQL levels as low as 0.040, and a commitment to personalized support from initial design concept through finished product. Statistical process control, PPAP, IQ/OQ/PQ validations, and real-time particle-contamination testing are standard practice.

Mark One Metal Works was founded in 1996 in Sparks, Nevada, by Mark, a fabricator whose career began in his teens as a transmission mechanic under his father John. After managing the fabrication department at a Peterbilt dealership in Reno, he launched Levco Transmission in 1991 and ran it for 15 years before selling to pursue off-road racing. He then led production at Torchmate, a CNC plasma cutting manufacturer, scaling its output significantly. That blend of machining, fabrication, CAD design, and artistic sensibility led him to establish Mark One Metal Works as a custom metal fabrication and design shop serving the Reno–Sparks area and beyond.

The shop provides a wide range of metalworking services: machining, welding (including TIG), tube bending, CNC plasma cutting on a Lincoln Electric table, and 2D/3D CAD design. It handles both one-off prototypes and production runs, producing items that span industrial fabrications, commercial architectural elements (railings, gates, stairs), residential furniture (desks, tables, doors, fixtures), off-road and hot-rod components, and custom signs, trophies, and awards.

Customers come from commercial construction, residential design, industrial manufacturing, off-road racing, hot-rod building, and the awards/recognition market. The company has fabricated everything from stair railings for commercial buildings to roll cages for UTVs and custom metal furniture for private homes.

Mark One emphasizes exceptional design, unmatched quality, and great customer service, positioning its “unique metal working concepts” and over 30 years of experience as differentiators. The founder’s rare balance of machining, fabrication, CAD, and artistic ability is cited as the reason the shop can take a project from concept to finished product in-house.

Marshall Dry Goods Co., Inc. was founded in 1944 by Hassel Marshall in Batesville, Arkansas. What began as a general dry goods store selling clothing, blankets, and yarn gradually shifted toward fabrics. In 1985, Marshall Bentley and his father, Larry Bentley, took over the business, and Marshall Bentley remains the owner today, having completed the transition to a 100-percent fabric operation.

The company now designs and manufactures its own fabric lines, offering more than 5,000 SKUs with a focus on 100% cotton prints in 45-inch and 108-inch widths. Production uses both conventional rotary and digital printing, supporting a library of over 4,000 exclusive designs that are refreshed weekly. Beyond cotton prints, the mill produces batiks, flannels, minky, fleece, broadcloth, muslin, and quilt batting in 80/20 cotton-polyester, 100% cotton, and 100% polyester blends, available in widths up to 120 inches.

Marshall Dry Goods serves quilters, crafters, and independent retailers across the United States through both wholesale and retail channels. Its wholesale division supplies fabric by the bolt to shop owners, while the online store and the Batesville brick-and-mortar location sell by the yard. The company also operates Marshall’s Quilt House, a retreat space across the street from the main facility.

The business emphasizes quality, value, and fast delivery, a commitment it has maintained through 80 years of operation.

Mathis Electronics was founded in 1980 in Asheville, North Carolina, as an electronics repair shop serving the elevator industry. The company transitioned to contract assembly of printed circuit boards and PCB engineering in 1986, adding a focus on LED lighting that remains a core specialty.

Production runs range from prototypes to high-volume orders, and order tracking is available from placement through delivery.

The customer base spans the elevator, LED lighting, and broader electronics sectors, with references from companies such as ERM Manufacturing, PTL Equipment, EECO, and SEES. Mathis also supplies boards for humidity controllers, low-voltage switchgear, and other industrial controls.

The company’s stated mission ties manufacturing excellence to a commitment to honor God, emphasizing integrity, structure, and a business model designed to reward customers, employees, and owners alike. Its differentiators are presented as comprehensive in-house testing, a lifetime warranty made possible by low return rates, and a flexible, small-company approach to communication and scheduling.

name: Medical Device Academy, Inc.
old_description: Are you a start-up device company that needs medical device consulting services and training for an FDA 510k submission?
about:
Medical Device Academy, Inc. operates from Shrewsbury, Vermont, as a fully remote quality and regulatory consulting firm. The company employs ten professionals who work virtually across the Eastern Time Zone, with consultants based in North Carolina, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Vermont.

The firm specializes in preparing FDA 510(k) submissions using the eSTAR template, FDA pre-submissions via PreSTAR, quality system implementation for FDA, ISO 13485, and MDSAP compliance, and internal quality system audits. It also provides FDA U.S. Agent services, CE Marking technical file preparation, Canadian medical device license applications, regulatory pathway analysis for U.S., European, and Canadian markets, and verification and validation test plan development. Training is delivered through a 510(k) course series and procedure-specific webinars.

Clients are primarily start-up and small-to-mid-size medical device companies, including international firms seeking U.S. market entry. The company focuses on entrepreneurs at the proof-of-concept stage who need guidance on regulatory strategy, budgeting, and efficient use of limited funding.

The firm emphasizes teaching clients to self-monitor compliance and avoid remediation.
